h: Steam Trains, Country Parks and a Medieval Mystery
p: Crazy golf is a fantastic warm-up for a day exploring Peterborough, a city with far more history and green space than many people realise. If you're planning to make a day of it, try playing your round first thing, then heading out to explore.

Ferry Meadows, part of Nene Park on the western edge of the city, is a huge country park with lakes, meadows and woodland. There are walking and cycling paths, play areas, a café and plenty of space for picnics, and in summer you can try watersports on the lakes. It's ideal for burning off any energy left over after your round of golf.

Steam fans and young Thomas lovers should head to the Nene Valley Railway, a heritage line running steam and diesel trains between Peterborough and Wansford. Wansford station is home to the railway's collection of engines and carriages, and the railway has a special place in the hearts of Thomas the Tank Engine fans thanks to the engine of the same name that lives here. It's a charming way to see the countryside, especially on special event days.

History lovers will enjoy Longthorpe Tower, a little English Heritage site on the outskirts of the city, home to a remarkable set of medieval wall paintings that survived for centuries hidden under plaster. Peterborough Museum in the city centre, housed in a historic building on Priestgate, has displays on everything from dinosaurs and Roman history to the city's more recent past.

Burghley House, a magnificent Elizabethan mansion just outside Stamford, is a short drive north, making a cracking add-on for a weekend away. Its grand stately rooms and deer park make a lovely contrast to an indoor morning of putting.
